start.text: A village plaza at noon. Two troupes face each other in a ring of neighbours; the crowd will judge wit and harmony. Rabe the leader nods to you: "Bring the men together."
start.speaker: rabe

choices.text: Pound the drums as loud as you can to frighten the rival troupe
Start a steady beat and let the others find it, one by one
choices.verse: Beat by beat we find each other

choices.text: Let every drummer play whatever he likes best

loud.text: The drums crash and the rival leader smiles; nobody is afraid. Somebody's baby starts to cry. Rabe taps your shoulder: "Noise is not music. Now, the speech."
loud.speaker: rabe

steady.text: Drum joins drum until the plaza throbs like one heart. The neighbours sway. Rabe raises his straw hat: "Now, a speech to open the day."
steady.speaker: rabe

solo.text: Ten rhythms tumble over each other and the dancers hesitate. It is lively, but nobody can clap along. Rabe covers one ear: "Now, a speech."
solo.speaker: rabe

kabary.text: A speech opens the day, and a speech needs a saying everyone knows. You begin: "One voice is a pebble, but many voices together are a ..."
kabary.speaker: you

tone.text: The rival speaker arrives late in a rumpled coat and bows. The crowd waits to hear what you will say about the other troupe, before the singing begins.
tone.speaker: rabe

choices.text: Joke about their crumpled coats and their long, slow walk
Say nothing of them and keep to your own song
Praise their long walk and invite them to share the plaza
choices.verse: Welcome, walkers from the far hill

renihira.text: Singers form a circle for the long harmony song. Young Ravao, proud of her bright voice, rises above the others and the chorus wobbles at the turn.
renihira.speaker: you

choices.text: Hush her sharply in front of everyone
Sing over her with the biggest voice you have
Soften your own voice and lead her back into the line with a nod

dihy.text: The dance begins. Rabe's nephew leaps, his straw hat slips and he lands in a heap. The crowd gasps, then waits. Everyone looks at the ring.
dihy.speaker: you

choices.text: Laugh loudest and point at the hat
Signal the drums to stop until he is on his feet
Step beside him and turn the fall into a deep bow the drums can follow

close.text: Evening comes. The closing piece must thank the plaza in one last line. The neighbours lean forward. What does the final line say?
close.speaker: rabe

options: We were the best by far
Thank you, plaza, and thank both troupes

verdict.text: The neighbours stamp, clap and call out. Both leaders shake hands in the middle of the ring. Then the plaza starts to hum the final chorus together.

endings.headline: The plaza sings along
endings.text: Wit and harmony together: both troupes bow, and the crowd cannot pick a loser.

endings.headline: A good day on the plaza
endings.text: The troupe is applauded and the speeches are remembered, though not every moment was gracious.

endings.headline: More noise than music
endings.text: The neighbours cheer politely, then drift home before the last chorus.
